text:
Elena: Quick sync — we need to decide sequencing for inference perf work this sprint. ACME pressing for lower P95 latency, infra says throughput/backpressure issues are causing cost spikes. Can we RICE-score and agree a sequence?

Samir: Short list from infra: 1) KV prefix caching for chat KV cache (low effort) 2) Priority queueing / request lanes + backpressure (medium-high effort) 3) Dynamic quantization profiles per model (medium effort) 4) Auto-batching tuning by workload (medium effort)

Jordan: I'll throw out quick RICE estimates format: Reach / Impact(1-3) / Confidence(%) / Effort(pw) then score = (R*I*C)/E

Jordan: KV cache: Reach=60k reqs/day, I=2.0, C=80, E=2 => score ~ (60*2*0.8)/2 = 48
Jordan: Queueing lanes: Reach=150k reqs/day, I=2.5, C=60, E=6 => score ~ (150*2.5*0.6)/6 = 37.5
Jordan: Quantization profiles: Reach=120k embeddings/day, I=1.8, C=70, E=3 => ~ (120*1.8*0.7)/3 = 50.4
Jordan: Auto-batching tuning: Reach=200k tokens/day, I=1.5, C=50, E=4 => ~ (200*1.5*0.5)/4 = 37.5

Maya: Numbers look reasonable. A few operational constraints: any change affecting KV cache or batching must have deterministic rollback and traceable eval prompts. Launch criteria we care about: P95 improvement validated on customer prompt set, <10% increase in per-token cost, canary to 5% then 25% before full rollout. SLA gating for Dedicated customers: lane-based throttling must guarantee isolation under overload.

Samir: Practical sequencing suggestion: do KV cache first (fast win, low effort), run canary + evals; in parallel start quant profiles (gives cost wins, moderate effort); queueing lanes after those two because it's higher complexity and touches routing / billing. Auto-batching tuning can land alongside quantization.

Elena: From PM/customer perspective: ACME specifically wants 30% P95 reduction for short-chat flows during peak. Sales says ACME will accept a Dedicated config if it guarantees isolation even if hosted improvements lag. That affects prioritization — queueing lanes become higher impact for revenue protection if Dedicated deal is on the table.

Jordan: If we bump queueing lanes for Dedicated-only customers, adjust Reach for that item down but Impact for $$ up. Rough alternate RICE: queueing (Dedicated): Reach=20k, I=3.0, C=70, E=6 => (20*3*0.7)/6 = 7 -> numerically lower but strategic revenue value higher. We should add a separate "business priority" multiplier for enterprise deals.

Maya: Agree. Suggest we add two axis to prioritization doc: RICE numeric and Strategic bucketing (Enterprise revenue, Regulatory risk, Self-serve CAC). For roadmap commit we'll use RICE + strategic tag.

Samir: Ops note: queueing lanes require changes to request router + tracing; estimate 3 sprints for core work and another sprint for canary infra. Dependencies: metrics for per-lane latency, per-tenant token accounting, and billing hooks.

Elena: Decision ask for this thread: approve immediate work order: 1) KV cache (sprint A) 2) Quant profiles + auto-batching (sprint A-B) 3) Queueing lanes (sprint C) with Dedicated fast-path option if sales signals ACME commit this week. Also approve RICE table + strategic tag for final roadmap doc.

Jordan: +1 on sequence. I'll update the RICE sheet and add the enterprise multiplier column.

Maya: +1 but add explicit launch checklist: canary test plan, eval prompt set, cost delta dashboard, rollback runbook. Put owners on each item.

Elena: OK assigning owners — Samir -> infra work (cache + queueing), Jordan -> RICE + metrics, Maya -> launch checklist + SLOs. I'll coordinate with sales on ACME commitment.

deploy-bot: canary:started: Canary for kv-cache feature toggled in prod for 3 instances (5% traffic). Logs -> https://internal.redwood/logs/kv-cache-canary

Samir: Seeing initial canary P95 drop ~18% on short-chat traffic, cost delta +2%. Pushing metrics to dashboard.

Maya: Nice. Keep canary at 5% for 24h with smoke tests, then promote if stable.

Elena: Thanks team — will record this as the sprint plan and add to roadmap doc. We'll reconvene if ACME confirms Dedicated purchase.
